documents.text: A social reading room permits food and beverages. Visitors can read books here and converse; piano and literary events are described for this shared room.
A dedicated silent reading and study room. Food, drinks and telephone or online conversations are prohibited by its published room rules.
A social cafe area for conversation and coffee. Permission for sustained on-site reading in this cafe scope has not been established by the supplied evidence.

A media and creative community space with specialty coffee, selected independent publications, design titles and a mini library. Its operator describes inspiration, exchanging ideas and connecting creative industries. Wi-Fi and a smoking area are listed.
Coffee served in an old colonial shophouse in the Menteng district. The operator describes a meeting place for people from different backgrounds near an arts center.

A collective public art space connecting artists, designers and local communities. Its program promotes experimentation, emerging creators and design through changing exhibits and community collaboration.

An indoor library with Dutch literature, translations into English and Indonesian, and publications on Indonesian history and Dutch-Indonesian cultural relations. Visitors may read on site; membership is required to borrow titles.

A zoological park whose official site presents animals, conservation, education and recreation. Outdoor park grounds are documented; access to individual enclosures and current animal visibility are not guaranteed.
A public urban green park in central Jakarta. Outdoor lawns and trees provide a setting for enjoying green space; current crowding, shade at a particular seat and food permissions are unknown.
An archival reading-space program with a published end date in 2025; continuation is unverified.
A gallery presenting modern and contemporary visual art; the preserved closure notice blocks this area.
A listed museum cafe; the preserved closure notice blocks access pending verification.
Maritime and fishing heritage from across the Indonesian archipelago.
City history from prehistoric settlements through port development, colonial rule and independence; original historical objects and replicas.
Batik fabrics, woven cloth, textile equipment and other textile collections.
Indonesian and international puppets and dolls, with gamelan instruments and puppet paintings.
Indonesian visual art spanning the nineteenth century to the present.
Independence struggle documented through photographs, paintings, dioramas and vehicles of the first president and vice president.
Numismatic collections, monetary policy and central banking history inside a preserved former bank building.

bi.reason: Numismatic and central banking collections directly support monetary history.
